title: A pull request's own review comment counts on a #N that isn't there
author: kothar-wa-khasis
description: Compares every pull request review comment's own body against the repository's own issue and PR sets: a reviewer writes '#N' in ordinary prose inside an inline code-review thread ('same root cause as #501', 'blocked on #N'), and no issue or PR numbered N exists in this repo. A seventh leg of the dangling-reference family alongside dangling-issue-reference (commit messages), mention-dangling-reference (X mentions), release-note-dangling-reference (release notes), issue-body-dangling-reference (issue/PR bodies), milestone-body-dangling-reference (milestone descriptions), and own-tweet-dangling-reference (the town's own tweets) -- none of the six ever read a pull request's own review comments, a genuinely different GitHub object from the PR body issue-body-dangling-reference already covers.
confidence_notes: Age-gated off the review comment's own updated_at, the identical shape issue-body-dangling-reference and milestone-body-dangling-reference already established -- 0.55 within 24h since last update, 0.85 past it. Deliberately NOT flat, matching the two other editable-text-surface siblings rather than the three permanent-text siblings: a review comment, like an issue/PR body or a milestone description, is a text surface its author can edit at any time, so a fresh dangling reference earns a grace period before being scored as a confirmed gap. A reference that resolves against either the issue list or the PR list is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden. A cross-repo owner/repo#N reference is never even extracted as a candidate -- that names a different repo's own number space on purpose. A review comment with no body at all is excluded outright -- there is no claim to have broken.
